benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Rose to about $105.60 on 12 Oct (Trading Economics), up roughly 0.8% on the day, as tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz continued (a VLCC struck off the UAE on 9 Oct, two more tankers hit inside the strait 10-11 Oct) and Iran's security chief called the US response to its Hormuz-reopening proposal 'insufficient.' Week-ago is the 5 Oct value from this site's own prior run.

note: Brent and WTI rose about 0.8-0.9% on 12 Oct amid continued Hormuz tanker attacks — the VLCC GEM NO.2 struck off the UAE on 9 Oct, and two more unnamed tankers hit inside the strait on 10 and 11 Oct — and Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei calling the US response to Iran's Hormuz-reopening proposal 'insufficient.' TTF and Henry Hub also edged up. Gulf of Mexico Isaias-related shut-ins continued easing over the weekend (last confirmed update: 68.76% on 10 Oct).
